rule: S136 / D33's order — the frozen core's DSR/PSR/PBO attacked five classes deep (DD-49); every finding classified into EXACTLY ONE of BREAK / ASSUMPTION-LIMIT / THEORY-GAP; an ASSUMPTION-LIMIT cites its assumption by paper section (RP-1); a BREAK carries its reproduction; the search for the papers' worked examples is recorded (RP-2). rigor.py stays BYTE-FROZEN — every BREAK is ROUTED to the gate, never fixed in place. D33 remains UNSIGNED beside this ledger.
reference: Bailey & López de Prado — PSR (2012) / Deflated Sharpe (2014) / CSCV (Bailey, Borwein, López de Prado, Zhu 2017). The frozen rigor.{psr,deflated_sharpe,sr0_deflated,pbo,per_obs_sharpe} attacked; the module is imported and READ, never edited.

ledger.knownAnswerProvenance: PARTIAL (RP-2): Bailey & López de Prado do not publish fully-reproducible worked inputs for DSR/PSR; the strongest independent known-answer is the purgedcv oracle (S94, already agreeing to |Δ|<0.02) plus the closed-form PSR for a symmetric-normal series (recomputed here). No printed worked example was reproduced verbatim; this is disclosed, not silently substituted.
ledger.headline: NO BREAK found under five attack classes — a LOWER BOUND, not a proof. 6 assumption-limits (each citing its assumption by section, routed as flag-don't-emit or acceptable-as-is), 3 theory-gaps (both readings shown).

findings.attack: closed-form PSR for a symmetric-normal series (Bailey & LdP 2012, Eq.7): PSR(0)=Φ(SR·√(n-1)/√(1+SR²/2))
DSR = PSR(SR0) identity (Bailey & LdP 2014, Appendix): deflated_sharpe(r,N,V) must equal psr(r, sr0_deflated(V,N))

findings.observation: psr(constant)=nan (nan → None via json_safe — a flag, not a fabricated number)
findings.assumptionCited: Bailey & LdP 2012 §1: PSR requires an estimable Sharpe, which requires σ̂>0. A constant series violates σ>0; the code faithfully emits nan (→None), which reads as 'not judgeable' rather than a fabricated probability.
findings.routed: ACCEPTABLE-AS-IS: nan→None already flags; an explicit refusal string would be clearer but is a render-layer improvement, routed to the gate, never a change to rigor.py.

findings.assumptionCited: skew/kurtosis need n≥3 (scipy); the code guards n<3 → nan EXPLICITLY (rigor.psr line: `if n < 3: return nan`). Faithful and guarded.

findings.observation: pbo(4×5 matrix, S=8)=nan (explicit t<n_splits guard → nan)
findings.assumptionCited: CSCV needs T≥S to form S row-blocks; the code guards t<n_splits → nan EXPLICITLY (rigor.pbo line: `if n < 2 or t < n_splits: return nan`).

findings.observation: pbo(identical cols)=1.0 — a deterministic value from stable argsort, not nan
findings.assumptionCited: Bailey et al. 2017 (CSCV) assumes DISTINCT candidate performances; behaviour under exact ties is unspecified. The code breaks ties by stable argsort (a deterministic but arbitrary tie-break). Both readings shown: (a) ties→arbitrary rank (the code's choice); (b) ties→undefined/refuse. Neither contradicts the paper.

findings.observation: psr(series with NaN)=nan (NaN propagates → None; never a fabricated value)
findings.assumptionCited: the input is assumed to be a clean return series (Appendix B); a NaN violates that. The code propagates NaN→None (a flag), it does not fabricate — faithful.

findings.attack: strongly autocorrelated (AR(1), φ=0.9) series — the i.i.d. assumption probed
findings.observation: psr(white)=0.9867; psr(AR(1) φ=0.9)=1.0000 — the code applies the i.i.d. σ-of-Sharpe formula unchanged; the AR series' effective n is far below its length, so the reported confidence is OVERSTATED
findings.assumptionCited: Bailey & LdP 2012 §1 & 2014 (DSR): PSR/DSR assume i.i.d. returns — the σ of the Sharpe estimator, √((1 - g3·SR + (g4-1)/4·SR²)/(n-1)), is derived under i.i.d. An autocorrelated series violates this; the code is FAITHFUL to the i.i.d. formula and does not (and per the paper need not) detect autocorrelation.
findings.routed: FLAG-DON'T-EMIT (routed to the gate, NOT a fix to rigor.py): a render-layer autocorrelation check (e.g. a Ljung-Box / lag-1 ACF flag) should WARN that the i.i.d. precondition is violated before a PSR/DSR is shown — the number is faithful but the CONFIDENCE is overstated on autocorrelated input. This is exactly V26's τ_int finding (the ledger already knows yields are autocorrelated); the fix is a caveat at the render, never an edit to the frozen formula.

findings.observation: skew=14.02, kurt(non-excess)=197.69; psr=1.0000; the denom argument (1 - g3·SR + (g4-1)/4·SR²) is floored at 1e-12 (rigor.psr uses max(·,1e-12))
findings.assumptionCited: the variance-of-Sharpe estimator can be non-positive for extreme skew (a known pathology of the Mertens/Bailey moment expansion). The paper does not specify behaviour when the estimator's variance goes ≤0. The code floors at 1e-12 (→ a saturated z→±∞ → psr→{0,1}). Both readings: (a) floor-and-saturate (the code's choice — never emits a complex/nan number); (b) refuse/flag when the variance estimate is non-positive. Neither contradicts the paper; it is genuinely unspecified.

findings.observation: pbo(S=8)=0.5143 (symmetric 4/4); pbo(S=7)=0.5429 (asymmetric 3/4 via half=S//2) — the code emits a value for odd S rather than refusing
findings.assumptionCited: Bailey et al. 2017 (CSCV) constructs S/2 IS and S/2 OOS blocks — S is assumed EVEN. For odd S the code uses half=S//2 (floor), giving an asymmetric (S-1)/2 vs (S+1)/2 split; it is faithful to the combinatorial machinery but the symmetric-split premise is violated. The engine only ever CALLS pbo with S=8 (even), so this is a latent input-domain limit, not a live defect.
findings.routed: ACCEPTABLE-AS-IS with a caveat: the engine's only call site is S=8 (even); an explicit even-S guard would be clearer but is a render/validation-layer improvement, routed to the gate, never a change to rigor.py.

findings.attack: the PBO estimator's sampling distribution under a true-Sharpe-0 null (S116, extended)
findings.observation: the committed s116PowerFix shows the across-seed SD ≈ 0.10-0.13 (dataset-to-dataset variance dominates), the powered mean ≈ 0.508 vs theory 0.5 (z≈0.6) — a single PBO estimate is inherently noisy at any power
findings.assumptionCited: the CSCV paper reports a point PBO without characterising its sampling distribution across datasets. V38/S116 measured it: the estimator is unbiased vs the 0.5 null (no break) but high-variance per single dataset — a property of the estimator, disclosed, not a contradiction of the paper.
